alternatives_considered.approach: Seed through the public Server Actions (signup/createGroup/createExpense) instead of direct inserts
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Actions need request cookies/sessions and redirect on success, making them unusable from a script and untestable under Vitest; direct inserts reusing hashPassword, splitAmount and the same activity-row shapes are deterministic, run in transactions, and are what the seed tests can assert on.

alternatives_considered.approach: Share one file-backed PGlite database between the seed and serve processes via PGLITE_DATA_DIR
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: TR-1 forbids any local disk that outlives a request and its proof rejects disk-persisting code; the README's memory-only local story is load-bearing, so the seeded rows must reach the serving process through the app itself, not through disk.

issue_snapshot.title: Activity feeds with seed data and deploy guide
issue_snapshot.body:
Everyone can trust the audit trail of what changed, QA can seed reproducible data, and a person can deploy from the README.

Person sees: per-group and cross-group activity feeds (filter chips, chronological rows with actor, action and timestamp, link-through to expense or group) with empty, loading, partial and error states, plus seeded data to click through. Contract: CONSUMES activity rows written by the expense, payment and member slices; DEFINES feed readers, the seed script in scripts/ and the README deploy guide; health endpoint documented for sdlc:ready. Constraints: TR-10 same-transaction before and after, TR-12 seed shape and deploy docs, TR-11 token set, accessibility and performance bar.

**Risk.** Audit and operability risk: expense-edited before and after written in the same transaction as the edit, immutable feed rows, dev-only seed guard, production secret guards.

**Out of scope**
- Password reset, native apps, receipts, recurring expenses, multi-currency, charts and notifications (all spec S-10 deferrals)
- Dark mode (explicitly deferred in the UI tokens)

Covers: TR-3, TR-5, TR-10, TR-11, TR-12
Part of #1.
Depends on #7.

## Acceptance (from the split)
- **IAC-1** Per-group and cross-group activity feeds list expense added, edited and deleted, payment and member events with actor and timestamp, filterable by all, expenses, payments and members with the filter preserved on retry
- **IAC-2** Editing an expense writes a feed entry in the same transaction carrying the structured before and after of exactly the changed fields (description, amount, date, payers, participants, split type and inputs, category, note)
- **IAC-3** sdlc:seed loads known-password users, every split type, a multi-payer expense, payments and a placeholder (dev-only wipe-and-reload, never production), and QA can log in as a seeded user
- **IAC-4** README covers one-command local run and from-scratch Vercel deploy (Neon database, env vars, migrations); main screens stay interactive under 1s with skeleton, empty and error states keyboard-accessible

## Decisions (recorded by the pipeline)

- **replan-project** by @Shivam-Fl (2026-10-04T16:12:18.702Z):
  Approve with three changes; keep everything else as it is. (1) Neon driver: use Drizzle's neon-serverless driver (a Pool from @neondatabase/serverless over WebSocket) when DATABASE_URL is set, not the http driver. The http driver cannot hold an interactive transaction, and creating, editing or deleting an expense must write the expense, its payers, its shares and its activity entry atomically (TR-8: never half-written). Update ADR-0002, the getDb() interface, and TR-2's proof: the Neon smoke test runs one transaction that rolls back on error and leaves nothing behind. (2) Store the split rule with the expense, not only its result: the split type on Expense, and on each split line the member's input as entered (exact amount, percentage or share count, and whether they were included) beside the computed share. The edit form reopens showing exactly what was entered. Balances still read only the stored payer parts and computed shares. Add it to the data model, the expense editor in docs/ui.md, and an ADR. (3) The spec says every change is recorded 'with who made it and what changed': an expense-edited activity entry stores a structured before/after of the fields that changed (description, amount, date, payers, participants, split type and inputs, category, note), written in the same transaction as the edit. Say so in TR-10 and the ActivityEvent model.
- **replan-project** by @Shivam-Fl (2026-10-04T16:25:43.988Z):
  All three changes are in; thank you. One addition, then I approve: the Pool's lifecycle on Vercel. A WebSocket Pool must not outlive the request that uses it on serverless (Neon's guidance for @neondatabase/serverless): getDb() on the Neon side opens the Pool for the request and closes it when the request's work is done, including after an error, and nothing holds a Pool or client at module scope. Say this in the getDb() interface in docs/trd.md and in ADR-0002. And since CI and QA run on PGlite only, add an invariant that no code may branch on which backend it is running against except getDb() itself, so a Neon-only code path cannot hide from the tests. Keep everything else as it is.
